bullets.title: Fed broadly expected to hike Sept 16; 3 more hikes priced through 2027
bullets.body: Market pricing has moved to ~85-90% odds of a 25bp hike at the September 16 FOMC meeting following hotter-than-expected August CPI (+0.29% core MoM vs 0.2% consensus) and PPI. Multiple shops (Wolfe, JPM, Piper, 22V) now expect hikes in September and December with the median dot likely showing 2 hikes for 2026. OIS markets are pricing ~3.5 hikes through end-2027. Fed Chair Warsh expected to strike a neutral-to-hawkish tone; hawks gaining influence with Waller flagging hikes on any disinflationary surprise.

bullets.title: August CPI hawkish but PCE details more benign; inflation remains sticky above target
bullets.body: August core CPI printed 0.29% MoM — the second-hottest reading of the year — driven by airline fares (+2.68%), lodging, wireless services (+5.9%), and communications. Core PCE tracking at ~23-25bp for August, with disinflation largely from shelter/software. Underlying inflation running 100bp+ above Fed target with no attribution to tariffs/shelter lags remaining. Hedgeye September CPI nowcast tracking ~3.54% YoY (+14bp acceleration).

bullets.title: Brent crude near/above $100 on Iran-Houthi escalation; diesel at all-time highs
bullets.body: Brent crude hit $108 intraweek (its highest since July) as Houthi forces seized the Yemeni port of Mokha, edging toward control of Bab al-Mandeb, and US forces destroyed Iranian tankers in the Gulf. Saudi production fell ~1.9M bpd to ~6.2M bpd (lowest since 1990). US diesel futures hit $5/gallon for the first time. Goldman flagged $120/bbl risk if attacks intensify. Wolfe sees no quick diplomatic off-ramp; base case is 'muddle-forward' equilibrium with sustained energy price pressure.

bullets.title: Global DM central bank tightening cycle underway — ECB, BoJ, BoE all moving
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags 8 of 9 DM central banks projected to hike by year-end. ECB raised 25bp to 2.50% and guided to more work; Taylor rule analysis implies DM rates ~100bp too low vs fundamentals. BoJ expected to hike 25bp next week to 1.25% with markets pricing further acceleration. BoE likely to hold at 3.75% at its September meeting (6-3 vote expected) but shift language toward November hike, with CPI potentially reaching 4%+ by early 2027.

bullets.title: Real GDP at 4.6% annualized — well above ~2% 'speed limit'; consumer spending must slow
bullets.body: 22V Research and Piper note Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracking 4.6-4.74% for Q3 real GDP, far above the ~2% speed limit consistent with non-inflationary growth. Consumer spending running +2.5% with AI capex at similar levels, yielding combined ~4.5% nominal growth contribution. The consensus view: consumer spending must decelerate from 2.5%+ to 1-1.5% to restore inflation toward target. Non-AI cyclicals (retail, transports, housing) likely the first to slow; housing affordability at 15th historical percentile with 30yr mortgages near 7%.

bullets.title: AI capex secular theme intact; Oracle OCI +121% YoY, MSFT tripling datacenter to 38GW by 2032
bullets.body: ORCL F1Q27: OCI revenues +121% YoY to $7.4B, booked $30B+ in new AI cloud contracts, RPO surged to $664B (+46% YoY), and 850MW of new capacity delivered. MSFT announced plans to triple compute capacity from 12GW to 38GW by 2032. OpenAI paused new $200/month ChatGPT Pro subscriptions due to Astra demand straining infrastructure. Compute market tightening with older-generation GPU contracts renewing at ~20% premium. Morgan Stanley models AI capex driving 0.6-0.85pp of GDP annually through 2027.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure bottleneck: power, land, and supply chain — not chips — are binding constraints
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks flag that the binding constraint on AI infrastructure has shifted from semiconductor supply to power, permitting, and construction. Political opposition is intensifying — 7 in 10 Americans oppose data centers in their communities, ~500 jurisdictions have enacted bans/moratoriums, and ~$156B in AI infra projects were cancelled/delayed in 2025. Morgan Stanley estimates ~0.85pp of 2.6% projected 2027 GDP growth is tied to AI capex — politically constrained capex would benefit hyperscaler compute owners via pricing power but slow broader adoption.

bullets.title: AI power TAM to $91B by 2030 (69% CAGR); 400V/800V transition accelerates 2028
bullets.body: UBS models AI server power TAM at $91.1B by 2030 (69% CAGR from 2025-30). Power system content per watt rises from $0.57 to $0.87/W. 2027 expected to be particularly strong: +65% YoY accelerator die growth, Rubin ~60% higher rack power, AMD shift to rack-scale. 400V/800V migration becomes the larger driver in 2028-29. Grid constraints and 800VDC delays pose a $500M-1B TAM headwind risk. UBS prefers TI and ADI over Infineon for power semis exposure.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury yields pushing toward 5%; bond market pricing sustained inflation
bullets.body: US 10Y yields hit 4.97% intraweek, the highest since October 2023, driven by hot inflation data, geopolitical oil shock, and heavy corporate debt supply from AI capex. JPMorgan technical analysis sees late-stage bearish trend exhaustion at 5.38-5.59% on 30Y bonds with potential mean reversion. 22V and PSC macro models suggest fair value near 5-6% given 6.6% nominal GDP growth. Bond-equity correlation is turning sharply positive, undermining 60/40 portfolios.

bullets.title: S&P 500 down ~0.8% on the week; AI/momentum factor up, non-AI cyclicals sharply lower
bullets.body: S&P 500 fell 0.8% for the week ended Sept 11 (after snapping two winning streaks), with breadth extremely negative — 80%+ of stocks down on key sessions. Equity Risk Premium compressed to 2.1%, lowest since 2002, implying higher rate sensitivity. Goldman noted TMT stocks saw the largest 2-week long buying since June 2025 (97th percentile). Positioning: hedge fund net leverage retreated to 52% (25th %-tile); shorts outpaced longs 2:1. Small caps (IWM) remain in bearish trend and trend; Russell 2000 -2.4% on the week.

bullets.title: Market rotation: AI buildout and momentum outperform; non-AI cyclicals, retail, transports lag
bullets.body: 22V and Goldman document a sharp rotation: AI buildout basket (semis, power, cooling) and AI services basket up 2%+ long-short over two weeks. Consumer Discretionary posted a technical breakdown with 59% of stocks showing Weak/Poor scores. Non-AI cyclicals (Retail, Transports, Housing) underperforming with housing stocks near decade lows. CTA crude oil positioning at 85th percentile; US bond CTA at 5th percentile. Homebuilder L/S ratio at 1st percentile since 2018.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit September 24; trade, tech controls, and Taiwan in focus
bullets.body: Presidents Trump and Xi are scheduled to meet September 24, with trade policy, technology export controls, Taiwan, capital flows, and supply chains expected to dominate the agenda. Jefferies is hosting a preview call on September 14 to discuss market implications. Separately, the US-China trade truce agreement expires November 1. AI technology restrictions and semiconductor export controls are the highest-stakes items for tech investors.

bullets.title: AI governance/safety discourse intensifying; Anthropic IPO mid-October at ~$2T valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO called for slowing frontier AI development on safety concerns; OpenAI CEO Altman backed the move and separately ruled out an IPO this year. NVIDIA reportedly considering investing up to $10B as anchor investor in Anthropic's IPO, which is reportedly targeting $100B raise at $2T valuation. AI safety governance legislation unlikely before December at the earliest. The AI extinction risk narrative is mainstream at the research/policy level, though market impact has been muted.

bullets.title: Semiconductor upcycle intact; memory prices surging, supply bottlenecks widening into 2027
bullets.body: Samsung/SK Hynix DRAM inventories fell below 10 days of supply. DDR5 RDIMM 32GB prices up 8.1% WoW and 13.9% MoM. NAND up 14% MoM. TSMC August revenue +53% YoY. UBS models global semiconductor revenues at $1.63T in 2026 (+118% YoY), $2.43T in 2027. Memory makers messaging 'extended tightness' through 2027. Apple raised iPhone Pro pricing $100-500 on memory cost inflation despite unchanged configurations, creating demand destruction headwinds in PC/Consumer/Auto/Industrial outside AI datacenters.

bullets.title: AI agents (Meta Muse, OpenAI Astra) seen as potential inflection point for AI trade; OTAs most exposed
bullets.body: Meta's Muse AI agent launched and hit #2-4 on the US App Store with early usage 10x internal test cohorts. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release was cited by multiple desks as reinforcing the AI infrastructure/compute trade. AI agents pose identified risk to OTAs (EXPE most exposed with 30-40% US hotel brand exposure vs peers' 3-4%; ABNB least exposed). Agentic commerce seen as potentially reshaping retail media, loyalty, and payments economics — but only ~1 visit per 600 retail site visits currently attributed to AI agents.

bullets.title: CHIPS Act quantum awards finalized; IonQ, RGTI, QBTS each receive up to $100M
bullets.body: The US Department of Commerce finalized $2B+ in CHIPS Act quantum computing awards: GlobalFoundries received $375M; IonQ, Rigetti (RGTI), D-Wave (QBTS), and PsiQuantum each received up to $100M. Government equity stakes lower future fundraising costs. IonQ also completed the SkyWater acquisition, raised FY26 revenue guidance to $450-460M (from $280-290M), and deployed its 256-qubit Superion platform with 330x cost-per-qubit improvement vs prior generation.

bullets.title: Software underperforming hardware/semis YTD; AI monetization inflection remains 2027-28 story
bullets.body: IGV is down ~0.7-4% YTD vs S&P 500 +12.7%. All-SaaS index trading at 5.5-5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales. Wolfe TMT conference highlighted AI monetization becoming real with consumption/credit-based pricing, but SaaS budgets growing mostly through security and coding. Enterprise AI adoption beyond coding remains very early-stage. Hyperscaler capex growth forecast to slow from ~60% in 2027 to ~12% in 2028 as compute capacity rises 4x — the market is watching for when the cycle turns toward software layer monetization.

bullets.title: OpenAI outpacing Anthropic on revenue; enterprise LLM spending flat August-September for first time
bullets.body: OpenAI revenue growth exceeded Anthropic in Q3 2026 with Codex driving 400-500% QoQ user growth. Anthropic ARR/revenue grew 142-145% QoQ in June; monitoring whether September slows to ~30%. Enterprise GenAI spend on global LLMs was flat August-September for the first time. Token prices falling sharply in an ongoing price war across 920 tracked global LLM models. Deepseek dominates agentic workloads. Negative on CRWV (neocloud build-out risks); GPU rental market quiet in August.
